html:
Neustria was the western part of the kingdom of the Franks in the early Middle Ages, between the Loire and the forests of today's Belgium, with Paris, Soissons, Orléans and Tours as its main cities. It is on the map for 600 and 700.

After Clovis died in 511 his sons split his realm, and Neustria and its eastern rival Austrasia often had separate Merovingian kings. Their feud reached a peak in the bitter war between the queens Fredegund of Neustria and Brunhilda of Austrasia. Real power slowly passed to the mayors of the palace. In 687 Pepin of Herstal, mayor of Austrasia, beat the Neustrians at the Battle of Tertry, and his family went on to found the Carolingian Empire.

Later the name meant a smaller march between the Seine and the Loire, held by the ancestors of Hugh Capet.
